summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes an obfuscated sibling payload
details: The package's preinstall script setup.mjs is written with obfuscator.io-style hex-mangled identifiers and per-function dispatch objects around fs/https/zlib logic. At install time it checks whether `bun` is on PATH; if not, it downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts the binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it (execFileSync) against the package-local math_init.js. math_init.js is a ~727KB single-line Bun-tagged bundle using a shuffled string-array decoder (rotator function that shifts a mixed numeric/char table) with hex-mangled identifiers and no readable strings, so its behavior is opaque to Node-based inspection. The package is advertised as a React micro-frontend utility library and has no stated need for an alternate JS runtime at install; running the payload under Bun (rather than Node) means standard Node lifecycle-script scanners never execute the delivered code. The combination of alternate-runtime dropper delivery, an obfuscated install helper, and an obfuscated Bun-only payload whose contents cannot be reconciled with the advertised library is the install-time-RCE fingerprint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
